title: SODA: Social Dialogue Quality Evaluation
description: Evaluate the quality of socially-grounded dialogues generated through social commonsense contextualization. Annotators rate naturalness, coherence, social appropriateness, and commonsense alignment of dialogues situated in specific social contexts and interpersonal relationships.
overview: Soda-Eval is a dialogue-quality evaluation benchmark introduced by John Mendonca, Isabel Trancoso, and Alon Lavie in "Soda-Eval: Open-Domain Dialogue Evaluation in the age of LLMs" (Findings of EMNLP 2024). It targets a gap in older evaluation benchmarks, which scored earlier chatbots on fluency and relevance rather than the failure modes of contemporary models. The authors report that modern models are usually fluent and relevant but still show recurring problems with coherence and commonsense knowledge.

The dialogues being evaluated come from SODA (Kim et al., EMNLP 2023), a million-scale social-dialogue corpus distilled from a language model by contextualizing social commonsense from the Atomic10x knowledge graph. Each SODA conversation is grounded in a short narrative, a relationship, and a head event. In Soda-Eval, turn-level quality assessments over these dialogues were generated with GPT-4, then used to benchmark and fine-tune open instruction-tuned LLMs as automatic evaluators.

Soda-Eval provides over 120,000 turn-level assessments across 10,000 dialogues, focusing on coherence, commonsense, fluency, and relevance. The underlying SODA corpus contains roughly 1.5 million dialogues, so the evaluation set is a small annotated slice of a much larger dialogue collection.

The Potato config below reproduces this evaluation task with five radio schemes rating naturalness, coherence, social appropriateness, and commonsense alignment, plus a free-text feedback field, each shown alongside the social narrative, the relationship, the head event, and the full dialogue. It is useful for collecting human quality judgments on model-generated social dialogue. The config's rated aspects adapt and extend Soda-Eval's set, adding naturalness and social appropriateness rather than fluency and relevance.
